title: Add rtpdump read and parse support
description:
Add a wiretap file format reader to read rtpdump files.
Generates "Exported PDU" data from the header of the rtpdump
file.

Add MIME file format read support for rtpdump files.

Change the default extension for exporting rtpdump files to '*.rtp' as
per the rtptools project's recommendation.

Wireshark generates rtpdump files slightly differently from how rtpdump
itself works. Both the wiretap reader and the MIME reader examine the
text and binary headers to determine the most appropriate presentation
of information to the user.

notes.body: All of these calls to `wtap_buffer_append_epdu_tag()` will need their third argument's typecast changed from `(guint8 *)` to `(const guint8 *)` once !10048 lands.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10050/diffs?diff_id=632162306&start_sha=3a41cf6894df719b048a111318b5240cfa9afa91#911bd75440ec6c1918a8ed2f1c2c66a41ee573bd_250_295)

> read rtpdump files as produced by Wireshark

Presumably you mean "as produced by rtpdump"; Wireshark doesn't define the file format, the [rtptools project does](https://github.com/irtlab/rtptools/blob/master/rtpdump.1), and if Wireshark doesn't produce files in the same format that rtpdump produces - and that rtpplay consumes! - that's a bug in Wireshark.

I did in fact mean "as produced by Wireshark"; specifically, as produced by the export function of the RTP player. Note that I did not say "as *defined* by Wireshark" as you seem to have interpreted the comment.

So will this also be intended to read rtpdump files as produced by, for example, rtpdump?  If so, why not just say "rtpdump files" without calling out a particular writer of rtpdump files?   Why is Wireshark worthy of note as an rtpdump writer here?

I specified Wireshark here because Wireshark generates rtpdump files and I wanted Wireshark to be able to read more of the file types it generates.

The reader can read files generated by rtpdump as well. You've surely noticed this by now when reviewing my work, but to make it explicit here for other readers, rtpdump repeats the destination address and port in both the text and binary headers, whereas Wireshark uses the text header to record the destination address and port, but the binary header to record the source address and port.

I feel the discussion of this discrepancy being a bug or feature is out of scope for this MR. Once you've made a decision and possibly patched the RTP export code, I'll update this MR to match.

I've revised the MR to explicitly handle rtpdump files generated by either Wireshark¹ or rtpdump.

* The comment at the start of `wiretap/rtpdump.c` documents the file format, including the differences between Wireshark's and rtpdump's treatment.
* The wiretap reader only generates source or destination address info if appropriate, based on heuristics to determine how much of this address info can be taken to be accurate. The logic for this can be seen in `rtpdump_open()`.²
* The MIME parser labels the header fields as text and binary instead of source and destination, and generates more accurate expert info explaining how likely the file is to be generated by rtpdump vs Wireshark.

¹ Of course, a lot of this logic becomes invalid if you end up making Wireshark's RTP export on par with rtpdump's.

² We could generate a file-level comment explaining the logic of why only some fields are shown and not others for the end user, but that seems like too much gold plating for the initial MR, even for me.
